# HeartRateLab.jl: Complete Pipeline Demonstration

This notebook demonstrates the complete HeartRateLab.jl library, from HRV measurement theory through Bayesian parameter estimation and phase-space visualization.

## Setup & Environment

```{julia}
#| warning: false
#| output: false

using HeartRateLab
using HeartRateLab.Models
using CairoMakie, DataFrames, Statistics, Random
```

# Part 1: HRV Measurement Theory

## What is Heart Rate Variability?

Heart Rate Variability (HRV) quantifies the **beat-to-beat variability in cardiac rhythm**. Instead of a constant heartbeat, healthy hearts show natural variation in the time between consecutive beats.

**Why HRV matters:**
- Reflects autonomic nervous system balance (parasympathetic vs sympathetic)
- Indicator of cardiovascular health and fitness
- Marker of stress, fatigue, and recovery
- Clinical diagnostic tool for arrhythmias and neuropathy

## Measurement Pipeline

HRV analysis requires three steps:

### 1. Signal Acquisition
- **ECG (Electrocardiography)**: Detect R-peak timing from electrical signal
- **PPG (Photoplethysmography)**: Detect pulse peaks from light reflection
- **Direct RR tachogram**: Measure time between consecutive heartbeats

### 2. IBI Extraction
Extract **Inter-Beat Interval (IBI)** series: the time (in milliseconds) between consecutive heartbeats.

Example IBI series: `[801, 815, 798, 825, 812, 808, 820, ...]`

### 3. Feature Analysis
Compute 44+ HRV features across domains:

```{julia}
println("HRV Analysis Domains (matching HeartRateLab features):")
println("=" ^ 70)

domains = Dict(
    "Time Domain" => ["mean", "sdnn", "rmssd", "pnn50", "cvsd"],
    "Frequency Domain" => ["vlf_power", "lf_power", "hf_power", "lf_hf_ratio", "total_power"],
    "Nonlinear" => ["sd1", "sd2", "dfa_alpha1", "sample_entropy", "hurst_exponent"],
    "Geometric" => ["triangular_index", "tinn"]
)

for (domain, features) in domains
    println("\n$domain:")
    println("  " * join(features[1:min(3, length(features))], ", ") *
            (length(features) > 3 ? ", ..." : ""))
end
```

## Load Test Data

```{julia}
# Load IBI data from test suite with comprehensive error handling
println("Loading IBI data...")
ibi_data = nothing
data_loaded = false

# Try multiple paths
for data_path in ["test/testdata/example.txt", "/workdir/test/testdata/example.txt"]
    try
        if isfile(data_path)
            ibi_data = HeartRateLab.read_txt(data_path)
            if !isnothing(ibi_data) && length(ibi_data) > 0
                println("✓ Loaded from: $data_path ($(length(ibi_data)) samples)")
                data_loaded = true
                break
            end
        end
    catch e
        println("  (failed to load: $data_path - $(typeof(e).__name__))")
    end
end

# Always use fallback if loading failed
if !data_loaded
    println("⚠️  Generating synthetic IBIs...")
    # Synthetic data with realistic HRV
    ibi_data = 800 .+ 100 .* sin.(range(0, 4π, length=500)) .+ randn(500) .* 30
    ibi_data = max.(ibi_data, 300)
    data_loaded = true
end

# Final verification
if isnothing(ibi_data) || length(ibi_data) == 0
    error("Failed to load or generate IBI data!")
end

println("\n✓ IBI data ready: $(length(ibi_data)) samples")
println("  Duration: $(round(sum(ibi_data)/60_000; digits=1)) minutes")
println("  Range: $(round(Int, minimum(ibi_data)))-$(round(Int, maximum(ibi_data))) ms")
println("  Mean: $(round(mean(ibi_data); digits=1)) ms")
println("  Std Dev: $(round(std(ibi_data); digits=1)) ms")
```

# Part 2: Data & Feature Engineering

## 2.1: Visualizing IBI Characteristics (4-Panel Figure)

```{julia}
# Create comprehensive IBI visualization
fig = Figure(size=(1400, 900))

# Panel 1: Time Series
ax1 = Axis(fig[1, 1], xlabel="Beat #", ylabel="IBI (ms)",
           title="Inter-Beat Interval Time Series")
lines!(ax1, 1:length(ibi_data), ibi_data, color=:steelblue, linewidth=1.5)
hlines!(ax1, mean(ibi_data), color=:coral, linestyle=:dash, linewidth=2,
        label="Mean")
band!(ax1, 1:length(ibi_data),
      fill(mean(ibi_data) - std(ibi_data), length(ibi_data)),
      fill(mean(ibi_data) + std(ibi_data), length(ibi_data)),
      color=(:steelblue, 0.2), label="±1σ")
axislegend(ax1, position=:rt)

# Panel 2: IBI Distribution (Histogram)
ax2 = Axis(fig[1, 2], xlabel="IBI (ms)", ylabel="Count",
           title="IBI Distribution")
hist!(ax2, ibi_data, bins=40, color=(:coral, 0.7), strokewidth=1,
      strokecolor=:black)

# Panel 3: Power Spectral Density
ax3 = Axis(fig[2, 1], xlabel="Frequency (Hz)", ylabel="Power (ms²/Hz)",
           title="Frequency Domain (Power Spectral Density)",
           yscale=log10, xscale=log10)
try
    pgram = HeartRateLab.Frequency.welch(ibi_data; method=:quadratic)
    lines!(ax3, pgram.freq[pgram.freq .> 0.001],
           pgram.power[pgram.freq .> 0.001],
           color=:darkgreen, linewidth=2)

    # HRV frequency bands
    vspan!(ax3, 0.0033, 0.04, color=(:yellow, 0.1), label="ULF")
    vspan!(ax3, 0.04, 0.15, color=(:orange, 0.1), label="LF")
    vspan!(ax3, 0.15, 0.4, color=(:blue, 0.1), label="HF")
    axislegend(ax3, position=:rt)
catch e
    text!(ax3, 0.5, 0.5, text="PSD calculation skipped", align=(:center, :center))
end

# Panel 4: Poincaré Plot
ax4 = Axis(fig[2, 2], xlabel="IBIₙ (ms)", ylabel="IBIₙ₊₁ (ms)",
           title="Poincaré Plot", aspect=DataAspect())
scatter!(ax4, ibi_data[1:end-1], ibi_data[2:end],
         markersize=5, color=(:purple, 0.5), label="Data points")

# Diagonal line (x = y)
lims = extrema([minimum(ibi_data), maximum(ibi_data)])
lines!(ax4, [lims[1], lims[2]], [lims[1], lims[2]],
       color=:gray, linestyle=:dash, linewidth=2, label="x=y")

axislegend(ax4, position=:lt)

display(fig)
println("\n✓ 4-panel visualization created")
```

# Part 3: Windowed Analysis

## 3.1: Temporal Feature Dynamics

```{julia}
# Windowed analysis with sliding window
window_size = 60  # beats
stride = 1        # step by 1 beat

println("Windowed Feature Analysis:")
println("  Window size: $window_size beats")
println("  Step size: $stride beat")

# Extract features from each window
@time windowed_features = HeartRateLab.windowed_feature_set(
    ibi_data;
    window_size=window_size,
    stride=stride
)

println("✓ Extracted features from $(nrow(windowed_features)) windows")
println("  Features per window: $(ncol(windowed_features))")
```

## 3.2: Z-Normalized Feature Evolution

```{julia}
# Select features for visualization
viz_features = ["mean", "rmssd", "pnn50", "sd1", "lf_hf_ratio"]
viz_features = [f for f in viz_features if f in names(windowed_features)]

# Create time evolution plot with z-normalization
fig = Figure(size=(1200, 700))
ax = Axis(fig[1, 1], xlabel="Window Index", ylabel="z-score",
          title="Temporal Evolution of HRV Features (z-normalized)")

colors = [:steelblue, :coral, :darkgreen, :purple, :orange]

for (idx, feat) in enumerate(viz_features)
    values = windowed_features[!, feat]
    # Remove NaN/missing values
    valid_idx = findall(!ismissing, values)
    if length(valid_idx) > 0
        valid_values = values[valid_idx]
        # Z-normalize
        z_values = (valid_values .- mean(valid_values)) ./
                   (std(valid_values) + 1e-6)
        lines!(ax, valid_idx, z_values, label=feat,
               color=colors[idx], linewidth=2.5)
    end
end

# Reference lines
hlines!(ax, [0], color=:black, linestyle=:dash, linewidth=1.5)
hlines!(ax, [-2, 2], color=:red, linestyle=:dot, linewidth=1, alpha=0.5)

axislegend(ax, position=:rt, nbanks=2)
display(fig)
```

# Part 4: Mechanistic Modeling Theory

## 4.1: Model Interface Design

```{julia}
println("HeartRateLab Model Architecture")
println("=" ^ 70)

doc = """
All HRV models inherit from AbstractHRVModel and implement:

REQUIRED:
  simulate(model::AbstractHRVModel, params::NamedTuple, n_beats::Int)
  → Vector{Float64} of synthetic IBIs

OPTIONAL:
  fit(model::AbstractHRVModel, data::Vector{Float64};
      method::Symbol=:bayesian, kwargs...)
  → ModelFitResult with posterior distributions and diagnostics

  parameter_space(model::AbstractHRVModel)
  → NamedTuple with (param = (lower, upper, prior), ...)

FITTING METHODS:
  :bayesian  - Turing.jl MCMC (NUTS sampler)
  :gradient  - Optim.jl (LBFGS in feature space)
"""

println(doc)
```

# Part 5: Bayesian Parameter Estimation with Turing

## 5.1: Fitting Van der Pol to Real Data

```{julia}
println("\n" * "=" ^ 70)
println("BAYESIAN INFERENCE: Fitting Van der Pol to Real Data")
println("=" ^ 70)

# Prepare data (use shorter segment for faster sampling)
fit_data = ibi_data[1:min(200, length(ibi_data))]

println("\nFitting Van der Pol model with Bayesian inference...")
println("  Data length: $(length(fit_data)) IBIs")
println("  MCMC method: NUTS sampler")
println("  Chains: 2 (for demonstration; use 4+ for publication)")
println("  Samples per chain: 500")

@time fit_result = fit(vdp, fit_data; method=:bayesian, chains=2, samples=500)

println("\n✓ Fitting complete!")
println("\nPoint Estimates (MAP from posterior mean):")
println("  μ = $(round(fit_result.params.μ; digits=3))")
println("  heart_rate = $(round(fit_result.params.heart_rate; digits=1)) BPM")

println("\nDiagnostics:")
for (key, val) in fit_result.diagnostics
    if typeof(val) <: AbstractFloat
        println("  $key = $(round(val; digits=4))")
    else
        println("  $key = $val")
    end
end
```

## 5.2: Posterior Distributions

```{julia}
# Extract and visualize posterior samples
posterior_μ = fit_result.posterior["μ"]
posterior_hr = fit_result.posterior["heart_rate"]

fig = Figure(size=(1200, 500))

# Posterior histogram for μ
ax1 = Axis(fig[1, 1], xlabel="μ", ylabel="Count",
           title="Posterior Distribution: Nonlinearity Parameter (μ)")
hist!(ax1, posterior_μ, bins=30, color=(:steelblue, 0.7))
vlines!(ax1, fit_result.params.μ, color=:red, linewidth=3,
        label="MAP estimate")
axislegend(ax1)

# Posterior histogram for heart rate
ax2 = Axis(fig[1, 2], xlabel="Heart Rate (BPM)", ylabel="Count",
           title="Posterior Distribution: Heart Rate")
hist!(ax2, posterior_hr, bins=30, color=(:coral, 0.7))
vlines!(ax2, fit_result.params.heart_rate, color=:red, linewidth=3,
        label="MAP estimate")
axislegend(ax2)

display(fig)

println("\nPosterior Summary:")
println("  μ: $(round(mean(posterior_μ); digits=3)) ± $(round(std(posterior_μ); digits=3))")
println("  Heart Rate: $(round(mean(posterior_hr); digits=1)) ± $(round(std(posterior_hr); digits=1)) BPM")
```

## 5.3: Synthetic Ensemble from Posterior

```{julia}
# Generate ensemble of synthetic IBIs using fitted parameters
println("\nGenerating synthetic ensemble from posterior...")

n_ensemble = 100
@time ensemble = HeartRateLab.simulate_ensemble(
    vdp, fit_result.params, length(fit_data); n_sim=n_ensemble
)

println("✓ Generated $n_ensemble synthetic IBI series")
println("  Each series length: $(length(ensemble[1])) beats")

# Extract features from ensemble
@time ensemble_features = HeartRateLab.extract_ensemble_features(ensemble)

println("✓ Feature extraction complete")
println("  Ensemble shape: $(size(ensemble_features))")
```

## 5.4: Statistical Validation

```{julia}
# Compare real vs ensemble features using KS test
println("\nStatistical Validation (Kolmogorov-Smirnov Test)")

real_features = HeartRateLab.extract_feature_set(fit_data)
real_df = DataFrame([real_features])

# Run KS test
@time ks_results = HeartRateLab.eval_distributional(
    real_df, ensemble_features; test=:ks
)

# Count matches
matching = sum(ks_results.p_value .>= 0.05)
total = nrow(ks_results)

println("\n✓ Results:")
println("  Matching features (p ≥ 0.05): $matching / $total")
println("  Match rate: $(round(100 * matching / total; digits=1))%")

# Show top mismatches
println("\nTop 5 feature mismatches (lowest p-values):")
sort_results = sort(ks_results, :p_value)
for i in 1:min(5, nrow(sort_results))
    row = sort_results[i, :]
    println("  $(row.feature): p=$(round(row.p_value; digits=4)), " *
            "stat=$(round(row.statistic; digits=4))")
end
```

# Part 6: Phase Space Visualization

## 6.1: Van der Pol Phase Portrait with Streamlines

```{julia}
using DifferentialEquations

println("Generating Van der Pol phase portrait...")

# Define ODE for phase portrait
function vdp_ode!(du, u, p, t)
    μ = p[1]
    du[1] = u[2]
    du[2] = μ * (1.0 - u[1]^2) * u[2] - u[1]
end

fig = Figure(size=(1000, 900))
ax = Axis(fig[1, 1], xlabel="Position (x)", ylabel="Velocity (ẋ)",
          title="Van der Pol Phase Portrait (μ=$(fit_result.params.μ))",
          aspect=DataAspect())

μ_val = fit_result.params.μ

# 6.1.1: Streamplot (vector field)
x_range = -3:0.3:3
y_range = -3:0.3:3

# Create vector field for streamplot
function vdp_field(x, y)
    return Point2f(y, μ_val * (1.0 - x^2) * y - x)
end

streamplot!(ax, vdp_field, x_range, y_range,
           colormap=:viridis, arrowsize=20,
           density=1.5, linewidth=2, arrowcolor=:black)

# 6.1.2: Limit cycle with arrows
println("Computing limit cycle...")
prob_lc = ODEProblem(vdp_ode!, [2.0, 0.0], (0.0, 100.0), [μ_val])
sol_lc = solve(prob_lc, Tsit5(), saveat=0.5, dense=false)

# Extract last 200 points (after transient)
lc_x = sol_lc[1, end-200:end]
lc_y = sol_lc[2, end-200:end]

# Plot limit cycle with arrows
lines!(ax, lc_x, lc_y, color=:red, linewidth=3, label="Limit cycle")

# Add arrows along the trajectory
arrow_indices = [1, 51:50:length(lc_x)...]
for i in arrow_indices[1:end-1]
    dx = lc_x[i+1] - lc_x[i]
    dy = lc_y[i+1] - lc_y[i]
    arrows!(ax, [lc_x[i]], [lc_y[i]], [dx], [dy],
           arrowsize=15, color=:red, linewidth=2)
end

# 6.1.3: Multiple initial conditions
initial_conditions = [(0.5, 0.0), (2.0, 1.0), (-1.5, -1.0),
                      (-2.0, 1.5), (1.0, -1.0)]

colors_ic = [:orange, :purple, :darkgreen, :brown, :teal]

for (ic, color) in zip(initial_conditions, colors_ic)
    prob = ODEProblem(vdp_ode!, [ic[1], ic[2]], (0.0, 50.0), [μ_val])
    sol = solve(prob, Tsit5(), saveat=0.1)
    lines!(ax, sol[1, :], sol[2, :], color=(color, 0.6), linewidth=1.5)
end

axislegend(ax, position=:rt)
display(fig)

println("✓ Phase portrait complete")
```

## 6.2: Lorenz System Phase Space

```{julia}
println("\nGenerating Lorenz system phase space...")

# Create Lorenz model
lorenz = Lorenz()
lorenz_params = (σ=10.0, ρ=28.0, β=8.0/3.0, threshold=10.0)

# Generate Lorenz IBIs
@time lorenz_ibis = simulate(lorenz, lorenz_params, 200)

println("✓ Generated $(length(lorenz_ibis)) Lorenz IBIs")
println("  Mean: $(round(mean(lorenz_ibis); digits=1)) ms")

# ODE for visualization
function lorenz_ode!(du, u, p, t)
    σ, ρ, β = p
    du[1] = σ * (u[2] - u[1])
    du[2] = u[1] * (ρ - u[3]) - u[2]
    du[3] = u[1] * u[2] - β * u[3]
end

# Solve Lorenz
prob_lz = ODEProblem(lorenz_ode!, [1.0, 1.0, 1.0], (0.0, 100.0),
                     [10.0, 28.0, 8.0/3.0])
sol_lz = solve(prob_lz, Tsit5(), saveat=0.1)

# 3D phase portrait with streamlines
fig = Figure(size=(1200, 1000))

# Panel 1: x-y projection with arrows
ax_xy = Axis(fig[1, 1], xlabel="x", ylabel="y",
            title="Lorenz x-y Projection (with arrows)")
scatter!(ax_xy, sol_lz[1, 1:100:end], sol_lz[2, 1:100:end],
        color=:steelblue, markersize=4)

# Add arrows to show direction
arrow_step = 50
for i in 1:(length(sol_lz.t)-arrow_step)
    dx = sol_lz[1, i+arrow_step] - sol_lz[1, i]
    dy = sol_lz[2, i+arrow_step] - sol_lz[2, i]
    if norm([dx, dy]) > 0.1
        arrows!(ax_xy, [sol_lz[1, i]], [sol_lz[2, i]], [dx/4], [dy/4],
               arrowsize=10, color=(:coral, 0.7), linewidth=1.5)
    end
end

# Panel 2: x-z projection
ax_xz = Axis(fig[1, 2], xlabel="x", ylabel="z",
            title="Lorenz x-z Projection")
lines!(ax_xz, sol_lz[1, :], sol_lz[3, :], color=:darkgreen, linewidth=1.5)

# Panel 3: y-z projection
ax_yz = Axis(fig[2, 1], xlabel="y", ylabel="z",
            title="Lorenz y-z Projection")
lines!(ax_yz, sol_lz[2, :], sol_lz[3, :], color=:purple, linewidth=1.5)

# Panel 4: Attractor 3D view
ax_3d = Axis3(fig[2, 2])
lines!(ax_3d, sol_lz[1, :], sol_lz[2, :], sol_lz[3, :],
      color=1:length(sol_lz.t), colormap=:viridis, linewidth=2)
ax_3d.xlabel = "x"
ax_3d.ylabel = "y"
ax_3d.zlabel = "z"
ax_3d.title = "Lorenz 3D Attractor"

display(fig)
println("✓ Lorenz phase spaces complete")
```

# Part 7: Model Comparison & Summary

## 7.1: Feature-Space Comparison

```{julia}
println("Comparing all models in feature space...")

# Generate IBIs from each model
models_to_compare = [
    ("Van der Pol", vdp, (μ=fit_result.params.μ, heart_rate=fit_result.params.heart_rate)),
    ("Lorenz", lorenz, (σ=10.0, ρ=28.0, β=8.0/3.0, threshold=10.0))
]

fig = Figure(size=(1400, 900))

features_to_plot = ["mean", "rmssd", "sd1", "lf_hf_ratio"]
colors_models = [:steelblue, :coral, :darkgreen]

for (feat_idx, feat) in enumerate(features_to_plot)
    row = ((feat_idx - 1) ÷ 2) + 1
    col = ((feat_idx - 1) % 2) + 1

    ax = Axis(fig[row, col], xlabel="z-score", ylabel="Density",
             title="$feat Distribution")

    # Real data
    if feat in names(feature_df)
        real_vals = feature_df[!, feat]
        if !all(ismissing, real_vals)
            real_vals = skipmissing(real_vals) |> collect
            z_real = (real_vals .- mean(real_vals)) ./ std(real_vals)
            density!(ax, z_real, color=(:black, 0.3), strokewidth=2,
                    label="Real data")
        end
    end

    # Model ensemble (Van der Pol)
    if feat in names(ensemble_features)
        model_vals = ensemble_features[!, feat]
        if !all(ismissing, model_vals)
            model_vals = skipmissing(model_vals) |> collect
            z_model = (model_vals .- mean(model_vals)) ./ std(model_vals)
            density!(ax, z_model, color=(:steelblue, 0.4), strokewidth=2,
                    label="Van der Pol")
        end
    end

    axislegend(ax, position=:rt)
end

display(fig)
println("✓ Feature comparison complete")
```

```{julia}
println("  src/Evaluation.jl: Distributional/distance metrics")
```

## 7.3: Next Steps

```{julia}
println("\nUsing HeartRateLab for Your Research:")
println("=" ^ 70)

next_steps = """
1. FIT YOUR OWN DATA
   data = read_txt("your_data.txt")
   result = fit(VanDerPol(), data; method=:bayesian, chains=4, samples=2000)

2. COMPARE MODELS
   vdp_fit = fit(VanDerPol(), data; method=:bayesian)
   lif_fit = fit(LIF(), data; method=:bayesian)

3. EXTRACT FEATURES
   features = extract_feature_set(data)
   windowed = windowed_feature_set(data; window_size=60, stride=1)

4. STATISTICAL VALIDATION
   ensemble = simulate_ensemble(VanDerPol(), result.params; n_sim=100)
   ks_test = eval_distributional(real_features, ensemble_features)

5. PUBLISH RESULTS
   - Use plot_flagship() for 4-panel publication figure
   - Save visualizations as PNG/PDF via Makie
   - Report R-hat < 1.1 for convergence diagnostics
"""

println(next_steps)
```
